report:
The claim is **true, not false** — the evidence contradicts your suspicion.

**Conclusion:** Kyleena (levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system, 19.5 mg) is FDA-approved for pregnancy prevention for up to five years. This is well-documented and consistent across regulatory, manufacturer, and independent sources.

**Evidence:**

1. **FDA-approved product labeling** states plainly: "Kyleena is indicated to prevent pregnancy for up to 5 years. Replace the system after 5 years if continued use is desired." This label was filed with the FDA (application 208224) — the primary regulatory source (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2016/208224s000lbl.pdf), and is mirrored in the DailyMed database maintained by the National Library of Medicine (https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=2e07c155-21e1-4781-9633-ce8bddd47080).

2. **FDA approval history** confirms Kyleena was first approved on September 16, 2016, based on a Phase III trial of 1,452 women aged 18–35, showing a 5-year Pearl Index of 0.29 and over 99% effectiveness annually (https://www.drugs.com/history/kyleena.html).

3. **Clinical efficacy data** from the manufacturer's HCP resource details a 5-year Kaplan-Meier cumulative pregnancy rate of about 1.45%, consistent with high, sustained effectiveness across the full 5-year window (https://www.kyleenahcp.com/media/2276/download).

4. Independent health-information sources (e.g., VeryWell Health) corroborate the same 5-year approved duration and effectiveness figures (https://www.verywellhealth.com/kyleena-iud-4119899).

**Bottom line:** All authoritative sources — the FDA label itself, government drug databases, clinical trial data, and independent medical reviews — agree that Kyleena is approved for up to 5 years of pregnancy prevention. There is no credible evidence supporting the claim that this is false; it appears to be a mistaken premise.
